title: Replying to @TalkinSpanglish #broadway #theatre #waitingforgodot #wes...
transcript: we now have an answer to the most important question surrounding this Broadway revival of Waiting for Godot starring Bill and Ted how will they pronounce the title of this play? for context this is one of the most contentious dramaturgical topics in the theatre canon most Americans learn this play title as waiting for guh-DOH but in England, and I think elsewhere they pronounce it as waiting for GOD-oh and of course this director, Jamie Lloyd, is British but the actors are American so it's kind of a toss up although for the record this Broadway revival in 2009 was in the same boat British director, American cast and they pronounced it GOD-oh and maybe even more significantly the most recent major revival in New York [at TFANA in 2023] had an all American team, including the director and they pronounced it GOD-oh as well and from what I gather, even in America, in more academic circles GOD-oh is generally considered the more correct pronunciation of the two I've even read some indication that Samuel Beckett himself pronounced it GOD-oh although I've had trouble finding hard proof on that in any case, this Broadway revival begins in a few days but we already have interviews with these actors where they pronounce it not guh-DOH but GOD-oh “but it's no Godot you've ever seen” “I had this strike of lightning that just said ‘waiting for Godot’” so to all of these people who lost their goddamn minds when I pronounced it GOD-oh in this video from last year I don't know eat your heart out? although if I'm being honest I do kind of go back and forth and in this video I said GOD-oh but after all the nasty comments I got I kind of felt like I just didn't wanna deal with it anymore because above all else of course I yearn to fit in and I crave the respect of people like TalkinSpanglish so I have been pronouncing it guh-DOH in other videos since then so whatever
